source_caption:
“You look stupid and rich” scene in Love Story is the perfect introduction to Jenny and Oliver because it turns flirtation into a verbal sparring match. She immediately sees through his polished Harvard confidence, and he’s drawn to the fact that she isn’t impressed — setting up a romance built on class tension, wit, and emotional honesty.

Love Story (1970), directed by Arthur Hiller, starring Ali MacGraw, Ryan O’Neal, Ray Milland. A timeless romantic drama about love, class, and loss, following two young people whose sharp chemistry grows into one of cinema’s most enduring tearjerkers.

source_details.synopsis: Love Story is a 1970 American romantic drama film directed by Arthur Hiller, written by Erich Segal (who concurrently adapted his screenplay into a 1970 novel). It stars Ali MacGraw and Ryan O'Neal, and features John Marley, Ray Milland, and Tommy Lee Jones in his film debut. The film is about a relationship between two students at Harvard College — the upper-class Oliver Barrett IV (O'Neal) and the working-class Jenny Cavilleri (MacGraw) — who are eventually affected by tragedy. The film was released by Paramount Pictures on December 16, 1970.
